intended_object: The ℤ-linear map from normalized integral singular cubical (n+2)-chains of X to π_{n+2}(X, x). It sends each cube whose whole boundary goes to x (so it is a generalized loop) to its homotopy class, and every other cube to 0. This is the cubical analogue of Eilenberg's map, used to invert the Hurewicz map. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body uses `Finsupp.linearCombination` to take the linear map on the free ℤ-module of (n+2)-cubes that sends c to `Additive.ofMul (basedClass x c)`. It then passes this map to the quotient by the span of degenerate cubes (`liftQ`), which is the normalized chain module.

`basedClass` gives the homotopy class of c when c is based at x (`IsBased`, which is equivalent to c being a `GenLoop`). For any other cube it gives the class of the constant loop, which is 0 in the additive group. So the map does exactly what the docstring says.

The map is well defined on the quotient because of `basedClass_of_isDegenerate`: a degenerate cube that is based at x is constant, so its class is trivial. This is the correct reason.

The degree is fixed at n + 2 on purpose. A ℤ-linear map into `Additive π_k` needs π_k to be abelian, which holds only for k ≥ 2. So this is the natural generality, not an arbitrary restriction.

Using ℤ coefficients is also part of the construction: a map from chains with coefficients in another ring to π_k does not make sense. Mathlib has no counterpart, since it lacks singular cubical chains and this Eilenberg-type map. Although the map serves the Hurewicz argument, it is a genuine mathematical construction, and it is formalized correctly.
